title: Pre-defined Functions and the Math Class

blocks.value: A function (or method) is a reusable block of statements that performs an operation. Pre-defined functions come built into Java's class libraries (like the Math class); user-defined functions are ones you write yourself.
To use a class's pre-defined functions, import it from its package — everything in java.lang is imported automatically, but others (like Scanner in java.util) need an explicit import.
Math class methods are static, so they're called directly on the class name — no need to create a Math object. Given double a = 3, b = 23, c = 34.45, d = 65.78; int e = -57;:

Method     Example           Result
abs(x)     Math.abs(e)       57
ceil(x)    Math.ceil(c)      35.0
ceil(x)    Math.ceil(d)      66.0
exp(x)     Math.exp(3)       20.085536923187668
floor(x)   Math.floor(c)     34.0
floor(x)   Math.floor(d)     65.0
log(x)     Math.log(a)       1.0986122886681098
log10(x)   Math.log10(a)     0.47712125471966244
max(x,y)   Math.max(a, b)    23.0
min(x,y)   Math.min(a, b)    3.0
pow(x,y)   Math.pow(2, a)    8.0
round(x)   Math.round(c)     34
round(x)   Math.round(d)     66
sqrt(x)    Math.sqrt(4)      2.0
A method's return value can be used directly in an expression: int x = Math.abs(-57); stores 57 in x. Using a method like this is called invoking or calling it.
